Hi Alex / Jordan —

Thanks for taking the demo today — really appreciated the candor on latency constraints for your fraud-detection paths. Quick post-call recap and the asks we discussed so we can align on Dedicated sizing and the SDK/auth work: 

Key notes from call:
- Two critical routes: (1) real-time transaction scoring (<= 150ms p95 target, single-request scoring) and (2) batch reranker for investigations (can tolerate higher latency, high throughput).
- Traffic shape: normal baseline ~120 qps, short bursts up to 1.8k qps for 30–90s during peak windows.
- Strict tenancy: StellarBank requires VPC private deployment and per-tenant concurrency limits.

Immediate asks (what we promised to deliver):
1) Capacity model: baseline vs burst sizing for Dedicated (GPU counts + queueing strategy). Attached: capacity_modeling_v2.xlsx (workbook).
2) Autoscale policy proposal: target autoscale window, cooldown, and burst buffer behavior.
3) SDK/auth checklist and routing approach (how you'd route real-time vs batch to different model variants and queues).
4) Short walkthrough on structured output/tool-calls for the scoring pipeline (schema enforcement + safe tool invocation).

Next steps we suggested on the call:
- We (Redwood) will send a recommended Dedicated config (HW, concurrency caps, queue settings) and a short SDK bootstrap + auth example.
- You’ll confirm whether the burst profile in tab "ObservedTraffic" matches your telemetry and share a sample 24h histogram if possible.

I’ve looped in Logan (runtime/ops) to sketch the autoscale/queue design in a follow-up message. Also attaching a draft SOW to capture scope.

Thanks Hannah — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we dig into the workbook: 

1) Baseline vs burst: the 1.8k qps peak is for a single region (us-west). We do have an overflow path to another region but prefer single-region first.
2) Concurrency caps: we require a per-tenant hard cap of 48 concurrent streaming generations for the real-time route. If you can provide guidance on per-worker concurrency and expected qps per worker that would help.
3) Tooling: for the structured output and tool calls — we need assurances around failure isolation (tool timeouts) and deterministic schema validation before writes to downstream systems.

Alex —

Quick technical sketch below to address the concurrency/qps mapping, autoscale, and SDK hookup. This is intentionally pragmatic so you can map to your infra metrics.

1) Concurrency -> QPS mapping
- Real-time route (short generation): we expect ~12–16 qps per GPU-dev worker at p95 when using the quantized model variant we demoed. That assumes batching window 10–15ms and target latency budget <=150ms.
- So 48 concurrent streaming generations ~= 3–4 workers (GPUs) for baseline; allow headroom for CPU-side overhead and KV cache warm-up -> baseline allocation = 6 workers.

2) Burst handling and queueing
- Approach: keep a small in-memory token-limited queue per route (circuit-breaker style). Allow burst buffer up to 8x baseline qps for short windows by spinning additional workers from a burst pool.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: scale-out threshold at 70% CPU/GPU utilization or 65% observed latency breach, cooldown 60s, scale-in after sustained 5m below threshold. Burst pool pre-warmed with 2 hot workers to handle first 30s of surge.
- Queue behavior: route request to either "realtime" or "async-batch" queue based on header X-Redwood-Route. If realtime queue depth > 40, apply graceful backpressure (429 + Retry-After) or route to degraded-model variant.

3) SDK / auth suggestions (bootstrap)
- Use short-lived mTLS tokens for VPC/private deployments + per-route API keys for tiered concurrency control.
- SDK snippet (pseudo):
  redwood = RedwoodClient(
    endpoint="https://private-us.redwood.internal",
    auth=ClientCertAuth(cert_path="/etc/redwood/cert.pem", key_path="/etc/redwood/key.pem"),
    route_overrides={"real_time":"/v1/generate?model=quantized-v2"}
  )

- Header conventions: X-Redwood-Tenant, X-Redwood-Route, X-Redwood-Request-Type (sync|async). Use X-Trace-Id for end-to-end latency tracking.

4) Structured output & tool-calls
- Enforce schema with a two-stage validation: runtime schema check in the SDK + server-side strict JSON schema validator before tool invocation. Tools run in a sandbox with a 2s timeout and an explicit error code. Failures bubble as structured error objects; no direct writes unless transaction acknowledged.

5) Next deliverables from us (by end of Tue):
- A draft Dedicated node count + queue parameter table aligning to the attached workbook.
- Example SDK bootstrap repo link + README.
- Redlined SOW template (Hannah to share).

If useful, we can include a short flame-graph of p95 latencies per worker for the model variant we tested.

Cheers,
Logan
